stories.headline: AI Compute Crunch Deepens: Blackwell GPU Rental Up 48% as Agentic Demand Outstrips Supply

key_facts.fact: Ornn Compute Price Index shows renting an Nvidia Blackwell GPU for one hour now costs $4.08, up 48% from $2.75 two months earlier, driven by agentic AI demand.
OpenAI's API token usage jumped from 6 billion tokens per minute in October to 15 billion per minute in late March.
OpenAI scrapped its Sora video-generation app partly to free up compute for coding and enterprise products tied to a new model codenamed Spud.
Anthropic has been hit by frequent outages and started metering Claude Code supply during peak hours.
CoreWeave raised prices by more than 20% and began pushing smaller customers into at least three-year contracts, up from one year previously.

OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar: 'I do spend a lot of time trying to find any last-minute compute available. We're making some very tough trades at the moment on things we're not pursuing because we don't have enough compute.'
Bank of America analysts argue demand will outstrip supply through at least 2029.

stories.headline: Sam Altman's Home Targeted in Second Attack; Two Suspects Arrested for Negligent Discharge

key_facts.fact: At 1:40 AM Sunday April 12, a Honda sedan stopped in front of Altman's Russian Hill property and the passenger appeared to fire a round at the Lombard Street side, per surveillance footage and security personnel who reported hearing a gunshot.
SFPD arrested Amanda Tom, 25, and Muhamad Tarik Hussein, 23, and booked them for negligent discharge. A search of their residence turned up three firearms.

The shooting came just two days after 20-year-old Daniel Alejandro Moreno-Gama allegedly threw a Molotov cocktail at the property on Friday at 3:40 AM, then made threatening statements at OpenAI's Mission Bay headquarters.
Moreno-Gama was booked into San Francisco County Jail on suspicion of attempted murder, arson, and possession or manufacture of an incendiary device.

No injuries were reported in either incident. After the Friday attack, Altman wrote: 'The fear and anxiety about AI is justified. We are in the process of witnessing the largest change to society in a long time, and perhaps ever.'

stories.headline: Over 70 Teams Complete Night Test for Beijing's Humanoid Robot Half-Marathon

key_facts.fact: Over 70 teams completed a full-scale overnight test from April 11 to April 12 at Beijing's E-Town Economic and Technological Development Area for the humanoid robot half-marathon
Over 100 teams are registered for the official race on April 19, nearly a fivefold increase from last year, including four international teams
The 21.0975 km course runs from Tongming Lake to Nanhaizi Park through city roads, racing circuits, and park terrain
Approximately 40% of teams plan to run fully autonomously; those completing the race autonomously may qualify for a Guinness World Record
Honor is entering two humanoid robots named 'Lightning' and 'Energetic Boy' featuring embodied AI with motion-control algorithms for high-speed movement
The test simulated all key race scenarios including track navigation, equipment coordination, and emergency response

stories.headline: FDA Approves J&J's Icotyde, First Targeted Oral Peptide for Plaque Psoriasis

key_facts.fact: The FDA approved Icotyde (icotrokinra), an interleukin-23 receptor antagonist, for moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis in adults and adolescents 12+ weighing at least 40 kg.
Icotyde is the first and only targeted oral peptide that precisely blocks the IL-23 receptor, replacing injections with a once-daily pill.
In head-to-head Phase III studies, approximately 70% of patients achieved clear or almost clear skin (IGA 0/1) and 55% achieved PASI 90 response at Week 16.
The approval is based on the ICONIC clinical development program spanning four Phase III studies with 2,500 patients; adverse reactions were within 1.1% of placebo through Week 16.
Psoriasis affects more than 8 million Americans; the new oral option addresses an unmet need for patients who fail topical treatments and are candidates for systemic therapy.

stories.headline: France and UK to Discuss Independent Hormuz Navigation Mission, Distancing From US Blockade

key_facts.fact: France's President Macron announced France would organize a meeting with the UK and other willing countries to discuss a 'strictly defensive' multinational mission to restore freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz.
Macron described the mission as 'separate from the warring parties to the conflict' and 'intended to be deployed as soon as circumstances permit,' distancing from the US blockade.
UK PM Keir Starmer said Britain would not take part in the US blockade but remained 'committed to reopening the critical waterway.'
A CBS poll found 59% of Americans feel the Iran war is going 'somewhat or very badly' for the US, with bipartisan majorities saying key objectives — including keeping Hormuz open — remain unmet.

stories.headline: Gallup: 50% of US Workers Now Use AI on the Job, Crossing Milestone for First Time

key_facts.fact: For the first time in Gallup's measurement, 50% of employed American adults say they use AI in their role at least a few times a year, up from 46% the previous quarter.
13% of employees now use AI daily and 28% report using it a few times a week or more, both figures rising.
65% of employees in AI-adopting organizations say AI has improved their productivity, but only about 1 in 10 strongly agree it has fundamentally changed how work gets done.
18% of all US employees say it is likely their job will be eliminated within five years due to AI or automation, up from 15% in 2025. In AI-adopting orgs, the figure rises to 23%.
27% of employees in AI-adopting organizations report disruptive workplace changes in the past year, compared with 17% in organizations that have not adopted AI.
Among large organizations with 10,000+ employees that have adopted AI, 33% report workforce reductions compared with 30% reporting expansion — a net negative.
Survey was conducted February 4-19, 2026 with 23,717 US employees.

stories.headline: MiniMax Open-Sources M2.7, First AI Model to Participate in Its Own Development Cycle

key_facts.fact: MiniMax officially released the weights of M2.7 on Hugging Face on April 12, making it the company's most capable open-source model and the first to actively participate in its own development cycle.
M2.7 scored 56.22% on SWE-Pro, matching GPT-5.3-Codex, and 57.0% on Terminal Bench 2.
The model ran over 100 autonomous rounds of scaffold optimization during development, achieving a 30% performance improvement through self-directed reinforcement learning.
M2.7 maintains 97% skill adherence across 40 complex skills (each over 2,000 tokens) and is the highest-ranked open-source model on GDPval-AA with an ELO score of 1495.

stories.headline: Oil Surges 7-8% Past $100 on US Blockade Announcement; Global Markets Decline

key_facts.fact: Brent crude jumped 7% to $102.24/barrel and US WTI surged 8% to $104.24/barrel in early Monday trading after Trump's blockade announcement.
Brent crude has swung from ~$70/barrel before the war in late February to peaks above $119 during the conflict; it closed at $95.20 on Friday before the talks.
Analyst Saul Kavonic (MST Marquee) said the blockade will cut up to 2 million barrels/day of Iranian-linked flows, returning the market to pre-ceasefire conditions.
European and Asian markets declined: France's CAC 40 fell 1.0%, Germany's DAX lost 1.0%, Japan's Nikkei 225 dropped 0.7%, and US futures pointed lower.
Rystad Energy chief economist said the blockade 'will raise prices' but called it a 'negotiation tactic, which eventually resolves into a full opening of Hormuz.'
Trump acknowledged oil and gasoline prices may remain high through November's midterm elections, a rare admission of political fallout from the Iran war decision.

stories.headline: OpenAI Secures First Permanent London Office With 544-Person Capacity at King's Cross

key_facts.fact: OpenAI signed a lease for 88,500 square feet at Regent Quarter in King's Cross (Jahn Court and Brassworks Building), with capacity for 544 team members.
The office is expected to open in 2027 and will more than double OpenAI's current UK headcount of about 200 across research, engineering, customer support, policy, and sales.
The move follows OpenAI's February commitment to make London its largest research hub outside the United States.
OpenAI paused its main Stargate data center project in Britain last week due to high energy costs and regulatory uncertainty.
London site lead Phoebe Thacker cited the UK's 'incredible depth of talent and a strong track record in AI' as a key reason for expansion.

stories.headline: Orbán Concedes Defeat as Magyar's Tisza Party Wins Supermajority in Hungary

key_facts.fact: Tisza secured 53.53% of the vote with 81.49% counted, projected to win 137 seats — enough for a two-thirds supermajority to amend the constitution. Fidesz-KDNP received 37.84%, projected at 55 seats.
Turnout was approximately 77.8% — a record high with 7.52 million out of ~8.1 million eligible voters casting ballots, the highest since the fall of communism.
Orbán conceded within three hours of polls closing and called Magyar to congratulate him, ending his 16 years in power.
Magyar, 45, a former Orbán loyalist, told supporters beside the Danube: 'Together we overthrew the Hungarian regime.' He pledged to steer Hungary back toward the EU.
UK PM Starmer called it 'an historic moment, not only for Hungary, but for European democracy.' The Kremlin loses an ally that had blocked EU funding for Ukraine.
A supermajority would let Magyar undo Orbán-era constitutional changes that weakened judicial independence and entrenched Fidesz control of political institutions.

stories.headline: Russia-Ukraine Easter Ceasefire Marred by Thousands of Violations on Both Sides

key_facts.fact: Ukraine's General Staff reported 7,696 Russian violations over the 32-hour ceasefire, including 1,355 artillery incidents, 115 assault operations, and 6,226 drone strikes. No air strikes were recorded.
Russia's defence ministry said it recorded 1,971 ceasefire violations by Ukraine overnight into Sunday.
Two people were killed in Russia's Belgorod region by Ukrainian shelling; two Ukrainian civilians were wounded by a Russian drone attack in Kharkiv region.
Kremlin spokesman Peskov called the truce a 'humanitarian gesture' and said Russian troops would resume fighting as soon as it ends at midnight (2100 GMT Sunday).
A Ukrainian soldier from the 65th brigade said Russian reconnaissance drones continued circling over Zaporizhzhia, blocking efforts to recover fallen soldiers' bodies.

stories.headline: SoftBank, NEC, Sony, and Honda Form Japan AI Alliance Targeting Physical AI and ¥1T Funding

key_facts.fact: SoftBank, NEC, Sony, and Honda have formed a new company to develop large-scale domestic AI foundation models, with each founding member holding more than 10% equity.
Additional investors include Nippon Steel, Kobe Steel, and major banks MUFG, Sumitomo Mitsui, and Mizuho.
The venture plans to hire about 100 AI engineers and will apply for NEDO government funding of up to ¥1 trillion (~$6.3B) for domestic AI projects.
SoftBank and NEC will lead model development, while Sony and Honda will deploy them across automotive, robotics, gaming, and semiconductors. Preferred Networks is expected to join engineering.
A core goal is developing 'physical AI' capable of autonomously controlling robots and factory automation.

stories.headline: SoftBank, Sony, Honda and NEC Launch Joint Venture to Build Japan's Own AI Foundation Model

key_facts.fact: SoftBank, NEC, Sony, and Honda have established a new company to develop large-scale domestic AI foundation models for corporate and industrial use
The venture plans to hire about 100 AI engineers, with SoftBank and NEC leading core model development
Additional investors include Nippon Steel, Kobe Steel, and major banks MUFG, Sumitomo Mitsui, and Mizuho
The consortium aims to expand into 'physical AI' for robotics control and autonomous driving, with Honda applying the technology in mobility
The venture intends to apply for government-backed NEDO funding, which has allocated up to 1 trillion yen for domestic AI projects over five years
Preferred Networks, a Tokyo-based AI company, is expected to contribute engineers to the effort

stories.headline: Trump Orders US Naval Blockade of Iranian Ports After Islamabad Talks Collapse

key_facts.fact: Trump announced on Truth Social that the US Navy would blockade all ships entering or leaving Iranian ports via the Strait of Hormuz, effective Monday at 10 a.m. ET.
CENTCOM said the blockade would be 'enforced impartially against vessels of all nations entering or departing Iranian ports' but would not impede ships transiting to non-Iranian destinations.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards said any military vessels approaching the Strait of Hormuz would be considered a violation of the ceasefire and 'dealt with severely.'
Iran's military called the blockade 'piracy' and warned that if Iranian port security is threatened, 'no port in the Persian Gulf and the Sea of Oman will remain safe.'

Vice President Vance said the core sticking point was Iran's refusal to commit to abandoning nuclear weapons, stating: 'We need to see an affirmative commitment that they will not seek a nuclear weapon.'
The status of the two-week ceasefire is now uncertain; Pakistan urged both sides to maintain it and said it would continue facilitating peace efforts.

stories.headline: Trump Threatens China With 50% Tariff if It Supplies Weapons to Iran

key_facts.fact: Trump told Fox News on Sunday that China would face a 50% tariff on all goods entering the US if caught providing military assistance to Iran during the war.
The threat follows US intelligence indicating China is preparing to ship air defense weapons (portable missiles targeting low-flying aircraft) to Iran via third countries.
Legal experts note the threat faces major hurdles: the Supreme Court struck down Trump's use of IEEPA for tariffs last February, and alternative legal tools require months-long investigations.
Trump is scheduled to visit Beijing in mid-May for talks with Xi Jinping; the meeting was delayed due to the Iran war.
China denied the allegations, stating it has not provided weapons to any party in the conflict and called the reports 'untrue.'

stories.headline: Rolls-Royce SMR Signs Landmark UK Contract for Three Small Modular Reactors at Wylfa

key_facts.fact: Rolls-Royce SMR signed a landmark contract with Great British Energy – Nuclear (GBE-N) for the design and delivery of the UK's first small modular reactors
Three 470 MWe pressurized water reactors will be built at Wylfa on Anglesey in North Wales, each powering approximately 1 million homes
The project will support 3,000 jobs at peak construction and thousands more across the UK supply chain
£2.6 billion was allocated in the 2025 Spending Review for the wider SMR programme delivery
BAM Nuttall, Laing O'Rourke and Atkins are part of the consortium developing the SMR design
Rolls-Royce SMR has also secured commitments for deployment in the Czech Republic and is in the final stage of selection in Sweden
The contract is part of the UK's broader nuclear expansion targeting 24 GW capacity by 2050, including a £14.2 billion investment in Sizewell C

stories.headline: Up to Half of Planned US Data Center Capacity for 2026 Faces Delays Due to Transformer Shortage

key_facts.fact: Sightline Climate report estimates 30% to 50% of approximately 16 GW of US data center capacity planned for 2026 will face delays or cancellations
Only about 5 GW of the 16 GW planned has actually entered the construction phase, while 11 GW remains at the 'announced' stage
Lead times for large power transformers have stretched from 24-30 months to 3-5 years, driven by competing demand from EVs, renewables, and grid modernization
Hyperscale cloud companies Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, and Microsoft have collectively guided for more than $650 billion in AI infrastructure capex in 2026
The US imported over 8,000 high-power transformers from China through October 2025, up from fewer than 1,500 in all of 2022
Looking to 2027, planned capacity reaches 21.5 GW but actual construction is only 6.3 GW

stories.headline: China's Victory Giant Launches $2.2B Hong Kong Share Sale as AI Server PCB Demand Surges

key_facts.fact: Victory Giant launched a Hong Kong share sale seeking up to HK$17.49 billion ($2.23 billion), offering 83.35 million shares at a maximum price of HK$209.88 each
Shares are due to start trading on April 21 under stock code 2476; 74% of funds raised will expand production capabilities in mainland China
Victory Giant ranked first globally by PCB sales revenue in AI and high-performance computing in Q1 2025, according to Frost & Sullivan
Cornerstone investors will buy almost $997 million worth of shares, led by CPE Rosewood, Janchor Fund and Jack Ma's Yunfeng Capital
The Shenzhen-listed shares surged roughly 583% in 2025 as investors piled into AI-related hardware names; the company was valued at about $37 billion
Victory Giant is a key Nvidia supplier and also counts Intel, Tesla, Microsoft, and Bosch among its clients; profits surged 273.5% in 2025
